newsitem.title: CHINA: Tibetan firm to issue shares in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Tibetan firm to issue shares in Shanghai.

text.p: A mineral water company will become the first Tibetan industrial firm to list its shares on the Shanghai stock exchange.
Tibet Shengdi (Holy Land) Company Ltd. said in the China Securities newspaper Thursday that it would soon issue 15 million A shares at four yuan (48 cents) each.
The company, which produces mineral water and also operates a hotel in the Tibetan capital Lhasa, will be the first industrial firm to issue shares from Tibet.

Few firms from the economically undeveloped areas in the west and centre of China have listed shares in stock markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen, which are dominated by companies in the richer east and south. But the "minority" shares have performed well.
Only one other Tibetan company, Tibet Pearl Star Co., a hotel group, has listed shares, but most of its assets are in the southwest province of Sichuan and not in Tibet.
Analysts said investors believe share issues from minority regions will receive preferential support from the central government, making them good targets for speculation.
"Investors are still keen on the minority share concept," said one broker with Guotai Securities.
"Holy Land has a good product in mineral water," said another broker. "If it was making refrigerators, then few people would buy it. Our water in Shanghai is polluted. We need good mineral water."
The firm, which has 310 workers, has annual output of 10,000 tons of "Himalayan Mineral Water," some of it transported by air to parts of China other than Tibet.
